claim: The line of the Japanese-held ground in China, 1940 to 1945, as drawn: the Yellow River bend, the Yangtze at Wuhan, the Zhejiang coast; the Ichi-Go advance through Henan (April to June 1944), Changsha and Hengyang (June to August 1944), Guilin, Liuzhou and Nanning (November 1944) and the link to Indochina in December 1944; the Japanese withdrawal from Guangxi in May 1945
source: From memory of the standard maps; to be checked against an atlas of the China theatre
note: The lines are schematic. The map says so under the drawing.

claim: The Japanese front in Burma: the advance from Thailand (January 1942), Rangoon (8 March 1942), the line at the Indian border (May 1942), the U-Go offensive to Kohima and Imphal (March 1944), the retreat to the Chindwin (July 1944), the Irrawaddy and Meiktila (March 1945), Rangoon retaken (3 May 1945)
source: From memory of the standard histories; the dates match the region timeline in the game

claim: The Japanese front on New Guinea: the landings at Buna and Gona (21 July 1942), Ioribaiwa (17 September 1942), the end of the fight on the north coast (January 1943), Lae and Finschhafen (September 1943), Hollandia (22 April 1944)
source: From memory of the standard histories

claim: The places of the reports (a city, a base or a battle), and the routes and landings drawn for 30 orders: the Kido Butai's northern route to Oahu, the Midway approaches, Kokoda, Guadalcanal, Leyte Gulf, Okinawa, the Doolittle raid, Corregidor, the Wake relief and others
source: From memory of the standard histories; the notes under the arrows say only what the order does
note: The staging places for Peleliu, Iwo Jima and Guadalcanal are loose, and Hainan as the origin of the southern Indochina landing is to be checked.
